flashcards.q: What problem do virtual threads solve, and what do they not solve?
flashcards.a: Thread-per-request scalability for I/O-bound work (unmount from carrier while blocked). They do nothing for CPU-bound work -- a CPU-bound virtual thread occupies its carrier for its full duration just like a platform thread.

flashcards.q: What causes a virtual thread to be pinned to its carrier, and which case did JDK 24 fix?
flashcards.a: synchronized blocks/methods (FIXED in JDK 24 via JEP 491) and native/JNI calls (still pins on JDK 25, unfixed).

flashcards.q: What does `sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Square` guarantee that pre-sealed-types Java could not?
flashcards.a: Compiler-enforced closed set of implementors, checked at compile time -- a switch over it can be verified exhaustive (no default needed, missing case = build failure). Before, this was convention-only (private constructor + comment), unverifiable by the compiler.

flashcards.q: What are records implicitly, and what can you NOT add to one?
flashcards.a: All fields implicit private final, canonical constructor, auto equals/hashCode/toString from ALL components. Cannot add a mutable field, cannot extend a class, implicitly final (no subclassing).

flashcards.q: How does ScopedValue differ from ThreadLocal, and why does it matter at virtual-thread scale?
flashcards.a: ScopedValue is immutable and auto-unbinds when the bound scope exits (no leak risk); ThreadLocal needs manual remove(). At millions of short-lived virtual threads, ThreadLocal's per-thread allocation cost becomes real; ScopedValue avoids it. Finalized in Java 25 (JEP 506).

flashcards.q: Is Structured Concurrency stable in Java 25?
flashcards.a: No -- still a preview API (JEP 505, sixth preview round in JDK 25). Claiming it's finalized/stable is a checkable interview mistake.

flashcards.q: Roughly how does throughput compare: pure reactive Netty vs virtual threads vs a traditional bounded platform-thread pool?
flashcards.a: Cited 2025-2026 benchmarks: pure reactive Netty ~200K RPS > VT-on-Netty ~150K RPS ~= VT-on-Tomcat ~140K RPS >> bounded platform-thread pool ~5K RPS (workload-dependent).

flashcards.q: What does `case Triangle(double base, double height) ->` do in a switch, and what JEP finalized it?
flashcards.a: Record deconstruction pattern -- binds the record's components directly as local variables in that branch, no accessor calls needed. Finalized as part of JEP 440 (record patterns) in Java 21.

flashcards.q: What is a carrier thread, and what happens on mount/unmount?
flashcards.a: A platform thread that runs virtual threads. MOUNT: virtual thread executes on a carrier. UNMOUNT: on a recognized blocking call (I/O), the virtual thread detaches, freeing the carrier to run a different virtual thread.

flashcards.q: When is Java 21 the right LTS target over Java 25?
flashcards.a: When the ecosystem (app server, legacy framework, vendor support matrix) hasn't certified 25 yet, or code accidentally relies on old synchronized-pinning-as-implicit-lock behavior. Otherwise 25 is the better default: extra JIT/GC years, Scoped Values finalized, pinning fix baked in.

flashcards.q: Why does creating a fixed platform-thread pool of 200 for I/O calls cap throughput regardless of downstream speed?
flashcards.a: Each in-flight call occupies a pooled OS thread (with its ~1MB reserved stack) for the whole blocking wait; with 200 threads and a 100ms call, max throughput is 200/0.1s = 2,000 req/s no matter how fast the downstream actually responds.

flashcards.q: Does virtual threads eliminate the need for concurrency limiting (semaphores/bulkheads)?
flashcards.a: No -- thread count is no longer the natural throttle it was with small platform-thread pools. A downstream's real capacity (DB pool size, API rate limit) still needs explicit backpressure even with virtual threads.
